newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE robusta coffee shaves gains by close.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE robusta coffee shaves gains by close.

text.p: London's robusta coffee futures shed slight gains in the early afternoon on origin and trade hedge selling but the market still ended broadly firmer, traders said.
Sentiment was supported by early trade covering.
But traders said London's reaction to rallying New York arabica prices was surprisingly muted.
"We have basically gone a different way to New York," said one trader. "In New York, people are a bit concerned about the low stock situation."
"Some of the premiums being paid for Colombian and Central American crop are too high to put it on the futures," he added.

"A lot of it hinges on the Mexican crop...The Mexican crop doesn't start coming through till November and the December contract goes off the board on December 17," the trader said. "Whereas London's got plenty of robusta being offered around," the trader added.
But others argue that there is also some concern over near-term robusta supplies, pointing to the steep November's premium to March in London.
By the midday close, November was $24 firmer at $1,519 a tonne after touching an intraday high of $1,525. January stood $12 higher at $1,440.
Volume totalled 4,014 lots. Traders said the Nov/Jan spread widened to close at the day's high of $79 against $69 on Thursday.
This week's rally in New York had been fuelled by the surprise 10,000 60-kg bag draw in the U.S. exchange certified stocks to 31,000 bags last week.

Further U.S. certified data are due on Monday. Traders said what is more important is the fact that there is no fresh coffee awaiting certification in New York. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
